title: For people reading reviews:
body:
I’ve just spent 2 hours downloading as many of these apps as I can find & trying out what features are free.

I’m gonna need you all to stop complaining cos I kinda wanted to as well but having spent the time looking I can confirm this app is giving the most out of all of them (for free)

99% of the other apps don’t allow you to repeat events/tasks without paying, for me that makes them unusable. Others were buggy with no support (per reviews) and one of them was a scam (didn’t fall for it luckily)

At least here the app functions as it should for free, and yesss I wanted more colour/graphic options for free as that is what is valuable to the neuro community, but at the end of the day it’s a business that needs to make money so it can provide the app. 

There was only 1 app I found that comes above this one for me, and you have to pay for repeating events😭 my advice to Thruday is to have a lifetime pay option, because ultimately the other app has won me over by having that option at £10 cheaper than your annual price, but you’ve got an amazing app and as you can tell I take research too far so I would know🤣

author: LewFreddie

title: Not a good start, we’ll see
body:
I just downloaded the app so I’ll update the review once I’ve used it longer but it’s definitely not starting off well for me. 
Firstly, as other reviews have said, their website (and the app description) is extremely misleading, it really highlights the fact that the app is free, without ever mentioning that some features are paid, which overall heavily implies that everything mentioned on the website is free. And the defensive replies from the developers on the reviews really don’t help (of course there are costs, no one blames you for it, just be transparent, because as it is your website *is* misleading).
Secondly, when I went to plan my day for tomorrow, it constantly changed the day to today (despite me selecting tomorrow or clicking a “free time block” from tomorrow).
So far, between the misleading information/lack of transparency and the bug it has been a pretty frustrating experience, but I’ll give it a go to see if it really is as helpful for AuDHD/Dyslexic people as it claims to be.
Please update your website and app description to make it clear that there is a free and a paid version, and what each version includes, so that people can find out this information before downloading the app and creating an account.

author: Appreview/90

title: Thruday Review
body:
Autistic Female 

Age:28 

I have never felt compelled to write an app review before,but I am so overwhelmed by the life changing abilities of this app that I felt I had to write this.

I downloaded it over a week ago,thinking it would take me a few days to figure it out,as normally that’s how my brain worked.

However the layout is simple to use,yet complex enough to cover various mental demands that my executive dysfunction brain requires.

For example the checklist action and the custom repeat option is essential for my task productivity and structure.

Within 24hrs this app had changed my daily routine into one of productivity and calm,as I gently switched from task to task that was on my schedule with plenty of time for rest.

I’ve had the most amazing week,with more time for leisure and hobbies instead of endlessly trying to micro-organise my life in case of mental lapses.

It’s a neurodivergent friendly interface,with enough options but not so many that you can waste hours scampering round and tampering with it(some productivity apps have overwhelmed me With their set up and consumed my time in trying to navigate them).

Plus it’s affordable at £50.00 for the year.

As someone going back to education,it’s a game changer for managing my time effectively.

And I haven’t even mentioned the traffic light mood tracker!

Or the breathing excercise section.

Or the Neurodivergent article links.

Everything has been incredibly well mapped out and considered for the user.

I can add my mum who is my carer so
She can have an overview of my day and my mood,which is so helpful on days when my verbal output is limited.

Thankyou so much to the team behind this app.

You have changed my life for the better.

Keep up the fantastic work

Ellie

author: LaureeHead

title: Such potential, but misses the key point for ADHD
body: This app should be a perfect fit for someone with executive function issues— it allows a person to create individual schedules with tasks broken down into steps, it gives the opportunity to create multiple reminders, and it has functionality that allows you to invite another person to support or manage your schedule. Unfortunately where it fails is pretty much on the most important point of reminders and checklists— the reminders pop up silently on your phone, with no audible sound or even a vibration. So unless you’re looking at your phone 24/7, you may as well have no checklist at all. Equally bad— it checks off the reminders automatically after the scheduled time has passed, not only removing the dopamine incentive that comes with checking something off your list, but also leaving people with short term memory issues unclear on whether they actually did or did not do a particular task. That said, this app has enormous potential, and I believe with some minor tweaks it could be the perfect partner for someone with ADHD. Selfishly, I hope the tweaks come sooner rather than later, because as another reviewer said, forgetting the cancel the trial just cost me (and my son, separately) $49 each for a year of something that is currently functionally useless to us both.
author: TeomRachel

title: Good app/ just not for me
body:
I like the free trial to test it out but don’t forget to cancel it on time like I did. It’s pretty easy to set up and use. I like the articles and mood tracker. The schedule works great too. I’m just not able to afford a new subscription due to the fact that I am disabled and social security is not enough to live on so I have to pinch every penny. 
I tried to stay on a schedule but I found that it wasn’t working for me and I started to ignore the reminders. I couldn’t find a way to snooze or mark it uncompleted either. I like to check things off my list to see my progress when I’m done. 
Thanks for letting me try your app and I appreciate what you’re doing to help neurodivergent folks like me. 
I’m just not ready to do without my pencil and sticky notes yet.
